Subject: Marketplace settlement routing and tax docs for co-sell invoice

Hi Evelyn,

Quick one — our finance team flagged that the AWS Marketplace invoice (attached: marketplace_invoice_aws_12345.pdf) shows the customer charge and a separate remittance line. We need to confirm how the settlement lands on your side and what documentation you need from us so we can recognize the expense correctly. Two things specifically: 

- For the US entity (Acme US Inc) we can provide W-9 if needed. Our EU subsidiary (Acme EU Ltd) expects reverse-charge treatment — do you need VAT registration evidence for that?
- For the co-sell split: the AWS invoice shows the full customer charge. Will Redwood be issuing an invoice to Acme for only your portion, or do we need a separate reseller invoice? Our controller is asking if there will be any credit memos / adjustments on your end.

Attached: marketplace_invoice_aws_12345.pdf (invoice stub), company_tax_profile.csv (list of Acme entities + tax ids).

Can we get a short list of documents you need (W-8/W-9, VAT cert, marketplace invoice number mapping), and an expected timeline for issuing any seller-side invoice we should expect? We want to close the bookkeeping loop before year-end.

Thanks,

Hi Jon — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. 

Short answer up front: we can support both flows, but the paperwork we need differs based on which Acme legal entity should receive Redwood's seller invoice and whether the customer charge is expected to be treated under reverse charge in the EU. Please see the checklist below — if you can return the requested items we’ll target a final settlement/invoice to you within 5 business days of receipt.

Required from Acme (pick which applies):
- If Redwood should invoice Acme US Inc: signed W-9 (for US tax reporting/payout setup).
- If Redwood should invoice Acme EU Ltd: copy of Acme EU VAT registration certificate + VAT number, and confirmation that the purchase is B2B and qualifies for reverse-charge.
- If Acme expects the reseller/entity split to be shown separately on customer paperwork, indicate which legal entity (name + tax id) should receive each line.

What Redwood will provide once we have the above:
- Settlement remittance file (we’ll attach the payout CSV) mapped to the AWS invoice number you provided.
- Redwood seller invoice for our portion (PDF). If you prefer a consolidated invoice for both seller and reseller splits we can discuss, but that often requires a reseller addendum.
- If adjustments are required (credits/chargebacks) we’ll raise a credit memo within our finance system and share a copy.

Notes on marketplace differences (short):
- AWS Marketplace (metered/transactable): AWS invoices the customer and remits to the seller; seller payouts are net of AWS fees. We issue our invoice to the legal entity you specify.
- Azure/GCP have similar concepts but different settlement timings and sometimes different documentation for reseller flows — if this deal spans multiple marketplaces we’ll coordinate per-marketplace evidence.

Can you confirm which Acme legal entity we should invoice and attach the relevant tax docs (W-9 or VAT cert)? If you want, we can set up a 30-minute call Monday to walk finance teams through the remittance file.

Best,

Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
T: +1 415-555-0199

Hi all — looping in Marketplace Ops/Finance playbook details so expectations are clear from our side. Sharing the operational steps we follow and the artifacts we will produce once Acme confirms the invoicing entity.

Operational checklist (Redwood marketplace settlements):
1) Confirm invoicing entity (legal name + tax id + payout bank details).
2) Receive tax docs from buyer/reseller: W-9 OR W-8BEN-E (if Acme is non-US and needs US withholding relief) OR EU VAT cert for reverse-charge.
3) Map AWS invoice number to our settlement report and generate:
   - redwood_settlement_template.csv (attached)
   - sample_marketplace_remittance.xml (attached)
   - Redwood seller invoice (PDF) for our revenue share line
4) If Acme requires Redwood to issue invoice to a different entity than the one AWS billed, we need a signed reseller addendum (DocuSign) authorizing the re-routing of settlement lines (link: https://www.docusign.com/ACME-Settlement-Addendum).
5) For EU VAT reverse-charge: we will include both Acme VAT number and a statement on the invoice referencing reverse-charge Article/Directive; Acme must confirm it is VAT registered and B2B.
6) Timing: typical turnaround after receiving complete docs is 3–5 business days; cross-marketplace (Azure/GCP) cases may add 2–3 business days.

Attachments provided by Redwood ops: redwood_settlement_template.csv, sample_marketplace_remittance.xml.

Next steps for Acme Finance: please send the preferred invoicing legal entity and attach either W-9 (US) or VAT registration evidence (EU) or W-8BEN-E (non-US foreign entity). If you want the seller share to be paid directly to a reseller entity, confirm that in writing and sign the reseller addendum — otherwise payments and remittance will follow the default marketplace remittance path.

Thanks — cc'd our finance team to expedite.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
